summary: Two special fourfold MMPs (birational to a Q-factorial target and semistable over a DVR), section extension and pl-flips, Witt-rationality and conditional lifting of threefold minimal models. Full main-paper reading; partial proof closure. Explicit source diagnostics obstruct treating the printed difficulty and surface finiteness arguments as closed proofs. General fourfold MMP, unconditional resolution and Picard lifting from numerical surjectivity are not claimed. A continuation recorded five verified source mistakes (sourceIssues E1–E5) and proved the fixed-coefficient version of Lemma 2.16 that Proposition 2.15 needs.

items.statement: The printed assertion that all ε-lc excellent surface pairs with at most m distinct resolution discrepancies have only finitely many discrepancy values cannot be used without a boundary restriction: for S={xy=z²}, C=(x,z), B=bC, 0<b<1/2 rational, ε=1/2 and m=2 work while the exceptional log discrepancy1−b/2 varies infinitely.

items.name: Finite discrepancies for ε-lc surface germs with fixed boundary coefficients (corrected Lemma 2.16)
items.statement: Fix m ∈ N, ε > 0 and a finite set I ⊂ [0,1). Consider ε-lc excellent two-dimensional pairs (S, B) whose boundary coefficients lie in I and whose minimal resolution at a point s has at most m distinct exceptional log discrepancies. Then these log discrepancies take only finitely many values. The printed Lemma 2.16, without I, is false (sourceIssues E2).
proofSteps: Let f: S′ → S be the minimal resolution at s, with exceptional curves C_1, …, C_k, r_i = dim_{k(s)} H⁰(C_i, O), C_i² = −r_ic_i and log discrepancies a_i ≥ ε. Write K_{S′} + B_{S′} = f*(K_S + B) with B_{S′} = f^{-1}_*B + Σ(1 − a_j)C_j. Minimality makes K_{S′} f-nef, so by the negativity lemma 1 − a_j ≥ 0.

The bounds on the graph are the source's own, from its [Kol13] citations: deg ω_{C_i} = −2r_i (3.30.2); a_iC_i² = (K_{S′} + C_i + (B_{S′} − (1 − a_i)C_i))·C_i ≥ −2r_i, so c_i ≤ 2/ε (the printed '−c_i' is a sign slip, E3); r_i ≤ 4 and C_i·C_j bounded (3.31, 3.41); the graph is a tree with at most one fork and three legs; and discrepancies are convex along legs (2.37), with equality forcing c = 2, f^{-1}_*B·C = 0 and both neighbour intersections equal to r.

New bound: since (K_{S′} + B_{S′})·C_i = 0 and (K_{S′} + C_i)·C_i = −2r_i, we get f^{-1}_*B·C_i = 2r_i + a_iC_i² − Σ_{j≠i}(1 − a_j)C_j·C_i < 2r_i ≤ 8. Also f^{-1}_*B·C_i = Σ_l b_l(B_l′·C_i) with b_l ∈ I∖{0} and B_l′·C_i ∈ Z_{≥0}. So it lies in the finite set F(I) = {Σ_b n_b·b : b ∈ I∖{0}, n_b ∈ Z_{≥0}, Σ n_b b < 8}. The printed proof tacitly treats these right-hand sides as bounded data; without I they are not (E2).

The equations (K_{S′} + B_{S′})·C_i = 0 are linear in (a_j), with coefficients C_i·C_j and constants 2r_i + C_i² − f^{-1}_*B·C_i − Σ_j C_i·C_j, all in finite sets. They have a unique solution because the intersection matrix is negative definite.

Along each leg the sequence a_i is convex, so its zero increments are consecutive. Hence each leg has at most one constant run, and otherwise each value occurs at most twice. With at most m values, collapsing each constant run to one variable leaves a leg with at most 2m + 1 variables. The removed middle equations hold automatically, since r_2(2a_2 − a_1 − a_3) = 0. The collapsed system is equivalent to the full system plus the equalities, so it has the same unique solution.

Up to relabelling there are finitely many collapsed systems: bounded size, coefficients in a finite set, finitely many combinatorial types. Each has at most one solution, so the a_i take finitely many values.

Application to Proposition 2.15, for n ≫ 0: localize (X_n, B_n) at a codimension-two C ⊂ Sing X_n. The boundary coefficients lie in the finite coefficient set of B, since flips do not change them. The minimal-resolution curves of the germ have discrepancy ≤ 0, so they are among the finitely many places E_1, …, E_m of discrepancy ≤ 0. That bounds the number of distinct values by m and gives ε = min(min_i A(E_i), min_j(1 − b_j)) > 0. The corrected lemma then rules out infinitely many strict increases of these discrepancies.

For X = {xy = z²} in characteristic > 5 and S = V(x, z), K_X is Cartier (index 1), while S has index 2 and Diff_S(0) = ½·{0}. The correct index is that of K_X + S, which is 2 here.
items.locator: Lem2.2 second clause; p5 image checked
proofSteps: For the same two-chart crepant resolution, f*S=S′+E/2; adjunction on S′ gives different1/2 at its intersection with E. The local ideal (x,z) has two independent generators modulo the maximal ideal, so it is not invertible at the vertex, while2S=div(x). The pair is plt from its snc log pullback. This supplies an explicit diagnostic, not a proof of the corrected general lemma.

Continuation: with m = index(K_X + S) = 2, the clauses 'mD Cartier for every D' (Cl = Z/2) and '(K_X+S)|_S = K_S + (1 − 1/m)P' both hold, confirming the log-index reading. The only consumer, Lemma 4.2, uses just the standardness of the different.

items.name: The node ruling has no Cartier multiple at its vertex
items.statement: For N=Spec K[x,y,z,w]/(xy−zw), the prime divisor D_K=V(x,z) is not Q-Cartier at the vertex. Consequently the T,D of node-ruling-family satisfy all the displayed hypotheses of Lemma6.6 but not its global conclusion; S is also smooth Q-factorial while T is not Q-factorial, contradicting the unrestricted global Q-factorial clause of Corollary6.7(1).
proofSteps: Use the small resolution in N×P¹ given by xt=zs and wt=ys. Its two charts are A³_(x,w,u), z=ux,y=uw, and A³_(z,y,v), x=vz,w=vy, with v=1/u.
It is an isomorphism away from the vertex, with exceptional P¹ and no exceptional divisor. The strict transform of D_K has local equations x and z, with z=ux on the overlap.

Its divisor line bundle restricts to O_P¹(−1), since the ideal generators transform by u. If mD_K were Cartier near the vertex, its pullback would equal m times the strict transform (there is no exceptional divisor), and its restriction to the exceptional fibre would be trivial. This contradicts degree−m for every positive m.

items.name: A primitive section avoids the entire special fibre
items.statement: Let T be integral and flat projective over a Noetherian DVR R with integral special fibre S, and let L be invertible. If H⁰(T_eta,L_eta)≠0, then there exists a section of L whose nonzero effective Cartier zero divisor does not contain S, or the zero divisor if that section is nowhere vanishing.
proofSteps: M=H⁰(T,L) is finite over R by proper coherent finiteness, torsion-free by flatness and invertibility, and nonzero by localization compatibility. Thus M is a nonzero finite free R-module.
Choose s∉πM. From 0→L --π→L→L|S→0, the kernel of restriction on H⁰ is exactly πM. Hence s|S≠0.
On integral T a nonzero section of an invertible sheaf cuts out an effective Cartier divisor; the nonzero special restriction means that S is not a component. No completeness or H² premise occurs.

items.name: Effective perturbations from numerical representatives
items.statement: In the projective lifting setting of Theorem6.1(2b), let f:X→Z be the prescribed flop contraction, H=f*H_Z for H_Z ample, and A the Q-Cartier strict transform of an ample divisor on its chosen flop. N¹_Q surjectivity supplies Q-Cartier representatives Hcal,Acal with Hcal|X≡H and Acal|X≡A. For m sufficiently large, some divisible multiple of mHcal+Acal has a section whose divisor does not contain X. Dividing by that multiple gives an effective Q-divisor Dcal with Dcal|X≡mH+A, hence Dcal is negative on the chosen flopping ray. This is a perturbation construction, not yet the full lifted-step theorem.
proofSteps: Lift rational numerical classes and clear denominators where sections are needed; do not claim equality with the prescribed line bundles.
H is nef and big because f is birational and H_Z ample. The generic lift is nef and big; for large m, mHcal_eta+Acal_eta is big and has sections after a positive multiple.
Use primitive-effective-section so that the divisor meets the special fibre properly. Restriction has the required numerical class. On the selected ray H has degree0 and A has negative degree.

With the standing strong resolution hypothesis, choose sufficiently small ε so (total,X+εDcal) is plt and (X,εDcal|X) is terminal by checking the finitely many coefficients on a fixed common log resolution.

Completion and H²=0 are not needed for this construction. Proving that the perturbed total MMP step has exactly the prescribed special flop still requires the boundary version of the lifted-step argument and numerical descent.

sourceIssues.locator: Lemma 2.2, second paragraph, p.5 of the published version (arXiv v2 Lemma 2.2, p.6)
sourceIssues.correction: m should be the Cartier index of K_X + S at P, the log index. For the plt surface germ obtained by localising at P, this equals the order of the local class group, and the conclusions then hold.
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample. Take X = Spec k[x,y,z]/(xy − z²), the A1 surface singularity with char k > 5, S = V(x, z), Δ = S and P the vertex. Then X is Q-factorial, (X, S) is plt and hence dlt, and P is a codimension-one point of the curve S. The minimal resolution (charts (x,z,y) = (u,uv,uv²) and (st²,st,s)) is crepant, so K_X is Cartier and m = 1. But div(x) = 2S and the ideal (x, z) is not principal at P, so S is not Cartier. Since f*S = S′ + E/2, adjunction gives (K_X + S)|_S = K_S + ½P, not K_S. With m = index(K_X + S) = 2 every clause holds. For a threefold example, multiply by A¹. The only other use is Lemma 4.2 (p.16), which needs only that the different of a plt pair with standard coefficients has standard coefficients; that is unaffected. Checked on the page image. Noted by the extraction (gap-index, item adjunction-index-diagnostic).

sourceIssues.locator: Lemma 2.16, p.13 of the published version (arXiv v2 Lemma 2.16, p.14)
sourceIssues.correction: Also fix a finite set I ⊂ [0, 1) and require the coefficients of B to lie in I. Then, over the minimal resolution, the exceptional discrepancies take finitely many values. This is what the proof of Proposition 2.15 needs, since the boundaries B_n of a flip sequence all have the coefficients of B.
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample. On the A1 surface S = {xy = z²} with C = V(x, z) and B = bC, 0 < b < 1/2, the minimal resolution is one (−2)-curve E, and K_{S′} + bC′ + (b/2)E = f*(K_S + bC). The pair is ½-lc for every such b (log discrepancies 1 − b/2 and 1 − b on an snc model with coefficients < 1/2), and there is one exceptional discrepancy, −b/2, so m = 1. That value varies infinitely. The proof fails because the right-hand sides B_{S′}·C_i of its linear system contain f^{-1}_*B·C_i, which varies with B. With coefficients in I the right-hand sides lie in a finite set, since f^{-1}_*B·C_i = 2r_i + a_iC_i² − Σ_{j≠i}(1 − a_j)C_j·C_i < 2r_i ≤ 8. Proposition 2.15 is unaffected. Noted by the extraction (gap-surface, item surface-finiteness-diagnostic); the corrected statement is proved in fixed-boundary-surface by this continuation.
